title: "Resources"
order: 2
---

External links for this lesson. All checked to load from a plain browser request as of the date
this page was written. (Note: eCFR's own site — ecfr.gov — blocks automated/proxied traffic with
a bot check, which is what this repo's build environment runs on, so its pages can't be
verified from here even though a human browser reaches them fine; the regulation text quoted in
this lesson instead comes straight from eCFR's public API, and the links below use two
verified-loading mirrors of the same official text.)

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR 606.160, current text](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.160)**
  — Cornell Law School's Legal Information Institute hosts a free, continuously updated mirror
  of the CFR. This is the live, current version of the exact section quoted in this lesson —
  regulations get amended, so use this to check whether the text has changed since this lesson
  was written, unlike the dated snapshot saved in this repo's `sources/` folder.

- **[Cornell LII: Title 21 browse index](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21)** — browse the
  whole title/chapter/subchapter/part/section tree this lesson's decoder table walks through, to
  see the numbering system in context.

- **[GovInfo: Code of Federal Regulations](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/cfr)** — the
  U.S. Government Publishing Office's official, legally authoritative annual CFR archive (PDF
  and XML, by year). This is where you go if you ever need the official, dated, legally citable
  version of a specific year's CFR text — for example, to confirm exactly what a regulation said
  on the date of a past inspection.

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR 11.10, current text](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/11.10)**
  — the live, current version of the second worked-example citation used in this lesson
  (Controls for closed systems, Part 11). Useful for the same reason as the 606.160 mirror
  above: a current check against the dated snapshot in this repo's `sources/` folder, and a
  preview of the Part 11 citation this curriculum returns to in the data-integrity module.
  Verified loading via direct request (HTTP 200) on the date this page was updated.

- **[Master the CFR: Researching the Code of Federal Regulations](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AYIEYSyMWtU)**
  (US National Archives) — a general tutorial on navigating the CFR system: the same
  Title/Chapter/Part/Subpart/Section/Paragraph structure this lesson's decoder table walks
  through, taught independent of any single regulation. Not blood-specific and doesn't mention
  Part 606 — watch it for the mechanics of locating a citation, not for anything about blood
  establishments. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed (HTTP 200, title and channel name
  confirmed) on 2026-11-11.
